problems: Caption says 'a black patch opens under them', but nobody goes through it: the dark patch is already there under the sheep in frame 1, and it only spreads into a flat dark stain with white crack lines. Sheep, crab and blue creatures all stay on top of it, so it reads as a shadow or paint, not a hole or broken ice.

The sheep, which stands on the patch at the start, slides out of the right edge of frame in storyboard frames 6-8 and is cut off by the frame (half a head at the edge in the 50% still). The main subject of the first second leaves without anything happening to it.
The pigs the caption mentions are mostly off-frame: in the first half only their legs or ropes show at the top edge, and at 50% and 75% the right-hand pig is cut off by the top of the frame.

The orange peanut-shaped object near the front blue creature (25%, 50%, 75% stills) hangs in the air beside the body with no hand or mouth holding it. At 75% a red rope runs from it to the creature's body. It is unclear what it is or what holds it up.
The blue creatures and the sheep slide over the surface without visible steps (storyboard rows 2-4). The sheep in particular drifts sideways while standing still.
The ropes are thick, glossy red tubes that rise in rigid straight lines up to the pigs (e.g. the vertical rope at the top of the 75% still), with no sag or weight. Nothing tells you they are rope.
The 'flecked dark water' is a flat dark plane covered in white oval stickers with the same pattern everywhere. It reads neither as ice nor as water, so 'thin ice' isn't legible without the caption.
The camera drifts and the frame is crowded at the top right, so the crab, the second blue creature and the patch cover each other. At 75% you can't tell where the hole is or what is happening.
posts.critique: Without the caption no one would know this is thin ice breaking: a dark stain spreads under characters who never sink, the sheep slides out of frame, and the pigs are cut off at the top. A floating orange object and footless sliding make it broken animation, not a failed experiment.
